PAPERS.title: Association of protein signature of fine particulate matter with MASLD: the underlying pathways and Mendelian randomization
PAPERS.pm: Annual average PM2.5 by bilinear interpolation, time-weighted; 700-protein elastic-net signature
PAPERS.n: 52,190 participants free of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease at baseline, 624 incident cases over a median 11.8 years. PM2.5 gave HR 1.19 (1.10-1.30) and a 700-protein elastic-net signature of PM2.5 gave HR 1.19 (1.08-1.31), the proteins enriched in NF-kB signalling and cytokine-receptor interaction; Mendelian randomisation supported CD28, CSF3 and HAVCR2 as causally associated with MASLD, and the signature mediated 15% (2.7-37.7%) of the PM2.5-MASLD association. Limitation: a 700-protein signature trained on the same cohort in which it is then tested will absorb variance from everything PM2.5 correlates with - smoking, adiposity, deprivation - so the mediated fraction is an upper bound, and its CI nearly spans an order of magnitude; the MR arm addresses protein-to-MASLD causality, not exposure-to-protein. Exposure is an annual mean from an interpolated surface, which is the weakest term in the chain. Relevance: moderate - liver endpoints are under-studied, and 15% mediation at best leaves the mechanism mostly open.
